title: I Took the Blacksmith-Forge Booking to the Mentor Who Left the Coal

parts.text: I lit forge 2 at 9:18 a.m. and mentor Cobb's coal was still banked on my unpaid-looking leftover. The board said: BOOK THE FORGE. BANK YOUR COAL. CLEAR THE HEARTH. I was forty, resident, holding a calendar hold. Cobb did not stop. "Mentors are the heat." I photographed the board, the hold, and his bank on my time. Then I logged an overlap. At 9:24 the shop lead pinged why Cobb's name was on my hearth. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop lead can see Cobb's banked coal on forge 2 during my booking.

social.video_title: The mentor left banked coal on my booked forge — Part 1/2
social.description: Blacksmith shop, a calendar hold, leftover coal. I logged the overlap. Would you have asked the lead?

parts.text: Cobb called it a heat until the lead asked for the log. I printed the overlap, the board, and the hold. He cleared the hearth. Cobb booked his own fire and told residents heats were always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when coal exists. Booking now has a second line: MENTORS CLEAR THE HEARTH. I keep forge 2. Cobb schedules. The shop finally looks like a hold, not leftover coke. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Overlap log, cleared hearth, and a second line. Was a heat ever my hold?
